correctness.rationale: For each arbitrary real sample vector the telescoping one-jump decomposition gives a sharp variation norm equal to the maximum of three step-polynomial variations. Rolle localization and the exact cubic derivative critical-value difference prove each closed branch for all strictly ordered nodes. For fixed half-gap a, the middle branch is strictly worsened by asymmetry; the appropriate end branch is no smaller, establishing strict global symmetrization. Differentiation gives opposite monotonicity of the two symmetric branches and a unique crossing with rational-enclosed root. Replayed symbolic checks, 400 independent numeric critical-point integrations and rational interval certificate support the algebra, without extrapolating finite tests into proof.

value.rationale: The sharp induced variation norm and its unique optimal sampling design answer a natural robustness problem for the first nonlinear-degree interpolant beyond affine variation preservation. Exact formulas over all asymmetric interior placements and three simultaneous extremal jump witnesses distinguish this result from isolated constant calculations; the best BV, best Lebesgue, and best monotone-range grids are distinct. This gives a concrete tradeoff in designing cubic interpolation for variation-sensitive data.
